title: Investigation of the Association Between Laboratory, Metabolic, Physiological, Lifestyle-Related, Radiological, Molecular Biological, and Microbiological Parameters with Postoperative Complications and Their Influence on Overall Survival and Recurrence-Free Survival in Patients with Oncological Diseases of the Esophagus and Stomach
summary: Background: Surgery for esophageal cancer carries a high risk of complications. Oral health and the composition of bacteria in the mouth and gut may play an important role. Research question: Can dental treatment before surgery reduce complication rates? Methodology: Patients with esophageal cancer are randomly assigned to two groups – one receives dental treatment before surgery, the other does not. Saliva and stool samples as well as clinical data are collected and analyzed.

Patients without preoperative dental rehabilitation (control arm): standard clinical care with a study-initiated diagnostic preoperative dental assessment, but without any dental intervention or treatment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age of majority (≥ 18 years)
Histologically confirmed malignant disease of the esophagus
Planned curative esophageal resection at the UKM
Capacity to provide informed consent
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal to provide study consent
Minority (< 18 years)
Inability to obtain biological samples
Medical or organizational reasons precluding study participation
